result.summary: Introduces descriptor inspection and multisig safety analysis to Bitcoin Core. The core analyzer inspects parsed descriptor key expressions and policy trees to determine whether a descriptor matches a recognized k-of-n multisig configuration (such as wsh multi/sortedmulti or single-leaf Taproot with NUMS or MuSig internal keys) and flags structural flaws such as duplicate keys or unintended spendable paths. This functionality is exposed via a new verbose flag on getdescriptorinfo and a new analyzedescriptor wallet RPC that matches descriptor keys against wallet-held keys, reports whether the wallet can sign, and computes first addresses.
result.problem: When joining a multisig wallet setup, participants receiving a descriptor from a coordinator must independently verify that it enforces the agreed k-of-n spending threshold, includes their key, and matches derived addresses. Core previously lacked programmatic policy inspection, requiring external tools to parse descriptor strings manually and risking acceptance of flawed descriptors (such as duplicate cosigner keys or active key paths) where fewer signers than intended can spend funds.
evidence: PR description: 'Before importing a multisig descriptor received from a coordinator, each participant needs to check that it is the setup they agreed on: a k-of-n where any k cosigners can spend and nothing else can, that their own key is in it, and that they all derived the same first address. Today nothing in Core reports what a descriptor commits to, so tools had to parse the descriptor string by hand, as the multisig wizard in #36325 (now closed) did.'

Commit ebc3c9f812: 'Two cosigner slots are the same holder if they share a root key, derive the same key at the first address, or one is the other's unhardened child xpub... Core accepts such descriptors, and fewer signers than the threshold can spend from them.'
result.scope_notes: The PR incorporates the first 3 commits from #35918. It also includes 4 commits authored by w0xlt for key and policy inspection, with detailed changes listed in the PR description.
result.changed_since_previous: Added a dedicated release note file (doc/release-notes-36885.md) covering the new analyzedescriptor RPC and getdescriptorinfo verbose argument.
result.card: Bitcoin Core adds descriptor key and policy inspection alongside multisig structure verification via AnalyzeDescriptor. Participants in multisig setups currently have no Core RPC to verify that a coordinator-supplied descriptor strictly enforces the intended k-of-n policy without hidden spending paths or duplicate keys that lower the threshold. The analysis is exposed without a wallet via getdescriptorinfo verbose, and with wallet key-matching and address derivation via analyzedescriptor. This PR depends on #35918 and advances the multisig setup workflow in #35645.

risk.why: A flaw in multisig analysis or wallet key matching could misinform users or automated tools about whether a multisig setup is safe before funds are sent to it.
